141: When I was your age, my squad started here with zero assumptions. We left route notes so unfinished training could be continued by the next session.
Until the current roster showed five active field detectives and one empty sixth position.

The routing log scrolls.
ROUTE FUNCTION: MATCH / ROUTE / VERIFY
CASE CREATION: NONE
FIELD POSITION 06: UNASSIGNED
So the system did not put the Cup back?
Good. That would have raised several technical questions.
The cases were real. The route could match a current case record to an unfinished training step. When we verified that step, it could reopen the archive material for the next one.
Exactly. And later, the old note and the plan. Real archive pieces, reopened at the moment the route needed them.
142: It could mark, match and route evidence.
It could not create a case, choose a suspect or solve anything for us.
Nini looks at the four answers you just entered.
Which is why every field came from work you already did.

The screen changes.
TRAINING ROUTE: COMPLETE
FIELD POSITION 06: READY FOR CERTIFICATION
Bibi looks at the Recruit Credential you chose to sign at the beginning.
The system could send an invitation to whoever held the book.
It could not choose your name.
143: So the empty place was real.
And you have the evidence to fill it.

The Academy could open the door.
Only you could earn the field badge.

THE SIXTH HOOK
Mimi sets the portable certification rack on the table.
The same rack you saw beside the Case Table when you claimed your Recruit Credential.
Five badges already hang in their places.
Hook 06 is still empty.
Nini looks at your Recruit Credential.
Luli looks at the completed maps.
Dilo looks at the final panel and very deliberately keeps both hands in his pockets.
Alio has brought the helmet. Nobody asks why.
Bibi turns the empty hook toward you.
145:
DETECTIVE ACADEMY // FIELD CERTIFICATION
AWARDED TO:
OFFICIAL CALL SIGN:
FOR SOLVING THE MYSTERY OF ROOM ZERO
BY FOLLOWING THE EVIDENCE ALL THE WAY TO THE TRUTH.
CERTIFIED FIELD DETECTIVE // FIELD SLOT 06
ROOM ZERO // CASE CLOSED
Signed: Happy Makers Detective Academy
Archive confirmation: BIBI // ARCHIVE MENTOR

Use the same call sign from your Recruit Credential. This certificate records what you earned; it is not another recruit card.

Mimi clips the badge to the rack.
Five occupied hooks become six.
They were already on the team.
I know. Now the paperwork agrees.
I have never respected paperwork more.
Enjoy the feeling. It will pass.

No fanfare is required.
Dilo tries a tiny victory noise. Nini adds an even tinier one.
Mimi is smiling too much to overrule either of them.
146:
For one whole minute, the Academy manages to be quiet.
Almost.
The team puts down its pencils. Bibi closes the Book 1 routing log and slides it into the archive tray.
Beside it is a small release flap.
Bibi points at it.
“That can wait.”
Dilo waits.
Technically.
Then he lifts the flap.
A dormant slot clicks.
A new file slides onto the tray.
This one does not carry the plain 0.
On the cover is a triangular archive symbol.
Luli freezes.
"Wait."
She flips back to the Look-Twice file from Case 03. The 017 / 071 mismatch sent them to older archive files. The symbol on this new cover gives them another question to record.
One changed number sent us to the archive.
And the archive still has more to tell us.
Case Three has returned from the dead.
Case Three is solved. This is a new question.
147: Which means we keep the archive trail open.

Inside is an old team photograph.
One person has been cut out.
On the back, in faded type:
RETURN BEFORE THE FIRST MEETING.
I recognize that file. I do not know why it has come back.
That was less than one quiet minute.
I have not even reassigned the helmet yet.
Detective, are you still with us?
120:
Mimi files the Guest House map.
After Reception confirms the handoff with Casey, staff finally open the parcel. Inside are transparent
overlay sleeves and old alignment clips borrowed long ago from Archive Restoration - exactly the
kind Bibi needs for delicate plan work.
Then the dormant routing light under the Case Table turns on.
For the first time since the torn note, the intake printer moves by itself. A narrow strip slides out:
MAP SET: COMPLETE
SELECTED FILES: 14
Nini turns to page 13 and taps the message you saved from Case 21. Around her, the fourteen files
named by the route are pulled from the case stack. Your Case 01 intake map stays clipped to the
recruitment file: it started the route, but it is not one of the fourteen selected for this step.
The old cases are about to become new evidence.
I knew we kept those maps for a reason.
I kept mine because the stack looked impressive.
Two reasons to keep the maps. Yours is very you.
Useful evidence and an excellent stack. Let him have both.
Then let me have some table. My elbow has become a paperweight.
